issues.description: The problem statement (and the solution) specify Meal constructor signature as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (UML and examples), but the template defines the constructor with the parameters in the reversed order: Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will make the provided example Main code inconsistent with the template and confuse students about the intended constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the template Meal.java to match the specification and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) { this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients; } and update any usages if necessary. This will align the template with the UML, problem examples, and the solution implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect the Meal constructor to have the signature Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first, ingredients second), but the template defines the constructor with the parameters reversed (Meal(String[] ingredients, String name)). This mismatch between the template and the problem/solution will confuse students and can cause compilation errors when they follow the example usages in Main or the constructor described in the task.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to match the problem statement and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) { ... } and update parameter names accordingly. Alternatively, adjust the problem examples to match the template, but aligning the template with the problem and solution (name first) is recommended.
